title: Dot products, norms and projections
objectives: Calculate real dot products and connect their signs to angles.
Normalize nonzero vectors and distinguish scalar from vector projections.
prerequisites: Chapter 2’s vectors, basis labels and matrix multiplication; elementary algebra. New notation is developed in the text.

quizzes.question: For nonzero u, when does u·v equal the signed projection length of v along u?
options: Only when v has unit length
feedback: For arbitrary u, divide by its length to get the signed component.
Correct. The direction vector must be normalized.
Normalizing v does not remove the scale of u.

quizzes.question: Can (0,0) be normalized to a unit vector by dividing by its norm?
feedback: Its length is zero, not one.
Correct. There is no direction to preserve and division by zero is undefined.
